transcript: Can I Be Frank? is a masterclass in blending comedy, commentary, and history. In a glorious 70 minutes, Morgan Bassichis embodies and pays tribute to the late gay comedian Frank Maya who died of AIDS-related complications while he was on the verge of a history-making big break. With a perfectly calibrated and knowing narcissism coupled with an unapologetically queer sensibility, this piece really distinguishes itself for me, reaching what I’d consider among the highest form of comedy. It's smart, layered, and emotionally resonant while maintaining a levity and ridiculousness that hits the hardest in a dark room full of people who are so ready to laugh. This is a love letter to a queer figure and queer history, a case for laughter when we needed the most, and a simply fantastic performance by Morgan Bassichis — I was truly impressed. Also, this is the third piece I've seen directed by Sam Pinkleton and between this, Oh Mary, and Ta-da, he's going three for three. Be sure to check out Can I Be Frank? which is running at Soho Playhouse through September 13th. With that, another program for my collection.
